meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 15: Versioning, Changelog & Lifecycle (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which statements about the Active / Deprecated / Removed lifecycle are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A Deprecated feature may be restored to Active by a superseding SEP
A deprecation requires a SEP that documents a migration path
Removal is decided by Core Maintainers once the window has elapsed
Removal from the specification forces Tier 1 SDKs to drop the feature
A feature is automatically removed in the first revision after its window ends

questions.explanation: Deprecation needs a SEP with rationale and migration path; removal happens at Core Maintainer discretion after the window; restoration is possible through a superseding SEP. SDK support timelines are governed by each SDK's own policy, and features may stay Deprecated far longer than the minimum.

questions.question: Which changes arrived in the 2026-07-28 revision? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: subscriptions/listen replacing the GET stream and resources/subscribe
Every result carries a resultType field
JSON-RPC batching, to reduce round trips on slow links
Mcp-Session-Id becoming mandatory on every POST

questions.explanation: A, B and C are major changes in the changelog. Sessions and Mcp-Session-Id were removed in the same revision, and MCP does not use JSON-RPC batches at all.

questions.question: Which of these are DEPRECATED in 2026-07-28 rather than removed outright? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Mcp-Session-Id and the session it identified
The initialize handshake that opened a connection

questions.explanation: Roots, sampling, logging and DCR are deprecated: still present, still working, removable no earlier than 2027-07-28. The initialize handshake and sessions were removed outright, together with ping, logging/setLevel, resources/subscribe and Last-Event-ID.
